main_text.l: Ratio: quia omnia peccata manent in infideli-bus, & merentur mortem.
Item: Christus & Paulus non solam infidelitatem, sed quævis peccata faciunt causam damnationis. Matth.25.1.Cor.6.
II. Negatur antithesis peccatorum & incredulitatis, quia[?] hæc est caput omnium peccatorum.
III. Per βλασφημίαν[?]: Si propter incredulitatem, Ergo propter peccata: Ratio quia incredulitas est pater & mater peccatorum.
Instantia. Incredulitas non consideratur ut in se peccatum est, sed quatenus respuit media salutis.
Resp. per βλασφημίαν quia respuit: ideo peccatum: quia contemtus salutis & mediorum est ἀνομία. Repudietur tam crassa ἀδολεσχία[?].
Argumentum II. à testimoniis Scripturæ, quibus beneficia mortis Christi ad credentes & Ecclesiam diserte restringuntur.
De credentibus. Ioh.3.16.&5.24.&6.40.47. Act.10.43. Rom.3.22. Gal.3.22. Heb.5.9. Ioh.12.46. ut nullus qui in me credit in tenebris maneat.
Resp. Imo addi, dum excluduntur infideles & alieni ab Ecclesia. Qui non crediderit, &c. Ergo soli credentes.

page.notes: The Greek words (βλασφημίαν in two places, ἀνομία, ἀδολεσχία) are hard to read at this scan resolution; the first βλασφημίαν occurrence is especially doubtful. "quia" in the second thesis has a mark over the u that is unclear. The left margin note reads "Huber.thef" with "1129." beneath it; "thef" is uncertain. "Argumentum" is set in italic run-in text, not as a separate heading, so it is kept as a paragraph. Ergo and the following "soli credentes." sit on separate lines as printed.
